In Oracle '' is NULL; in PostgreSQL it is an empty string that is not NULL, so comparisons, concatenations and IS NULL tests silently behave differently.
findings.fix_hint: write NULL where NULL is meant; if an empty string is meant, test for it explicitly (x IS NULL OR x = '')

findings.rationale: PostgreSQL has no DBMS_OUTPUT package; PL/pgSQL reports messages with RAISE.
In Oracle SYSDATE is a DATE and `sysdate - d` is a number of days; in PostgreSQL the same subtraction gives an interval and `+ 1` is an error.
findings.fix_hint: CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, LOCALTIMESTAMP or CURRENT_DATE, depending on the type needed; review the date arithmetic around it

PostgreSQL has no DECODE(); it is a CASE expression. DECODE also treats NULL as equal to NULL, which CASE x WHEN NULL never does.
findings.fix_hint: CASE expr WHEN s1 THEN r1 ... ELSE default END; use CASE WHEN expr IS NULL ... for a NULL search value
